headline: US military confirms it has deployed weapons in orbit for the first time
summary: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink publicly declared the existence of "on-orbit space control weapons" designed to defend US forces, a move expected to resonate in Beijing and Moscow.
details: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink announced Monday that the United States has placed "on-orbit space control weapons" in orbit. This marks the first public declaration of such a deployment, capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.

While Space Force officials had previously expressed interest in acquiring space-based weapons, and Pentagon leaders have become more open to discussing space warfare, the specific details of these weapons remain undisclosed. Meink did not reveal their nature or when they were deployed.

The disclosure signifies a notable shift in the Pentagon's stance on orbital warfare, a topic senior officials were reluctant to discuss publicly until recently. Military leaders now openly discuss orbital combat, defensive satellite countermeasures, and ground-based anti-satellite weapons.

Meink emphasized the importance of deterrence, stating that revealing specifics about the weapons, including testing details, would not benefit this strategic goal. He highlighted the critical nature of the space environment for military and economic security.

The US acknowledgement follows concerns over Russia's anti-satellite weapon tests in 2020 and accusations of operational deployment in 2024. China also operates highly maneuverable satellites viewed with suspicion by US military officials.

These Chinese satellites routinely maneuver close to US military assets, likely for surveillance, demonstrating advanced technological and operational acumen that could support a formidable counterspace arsenal. Meink defended the US deployment by citing these advancements by China and Russia.
caption:
The US military has officially confirmed it has deployed space control weapons in orbit.

Air Force Secretary Troy Meink announced Monday that the United States has placed "on-orbit space control weapons" in orbit. This marks the first public declaration of such a deployment, capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.

While Space Force officials had previously expressed interest in acquiring space-based weapons, and Pentagon leaders have become more open to discussing space warfare, the specific details of these weapons remain undisclosed. Meink did not reveal their nature or when they were deployed.

The disclosure signifies a notable shift in the Pentagon's stance on orbital warfare, a topic senior officials were reluctant to discuss publicly until recently. Military leaders now openly discuss orbital combat, defensive satellite countermeasures, and ground-based anti-satellite weapons.

Meink emphasized the importance of deterrence, stating that revealing specifics about the weapons, including testing details, would not benefit this strategic goal. He highlighted the critical nature of the space environment for military and economic security.

The US acknowledgement follows concerns over Russia's anti-satellite weapon tests in 2020 and accusations of operational deployment in 2024. China also operates highly maneuverable satellites viewed with suspicion by US military officials.

These Chinese satellites routinely maneuver close to US military assets, likely for surveillance, demonstrating advanced technological and operational acumen that could support a formidable counterspace arsenal. Meink defended the US deployment by citing these advancements by China and Russia.
